caption: This drawing depicts the interior of a mortuary or funeral home, characterized by a variety of objects associated with funerals. Dominating the left side is an ornate gray funeral carriage with decorative curtains and classical motifs. In the foreground, a large wicker basket is topped with a pair of black shoes, a pair of brown shoes, a hat, and a striped tie. Centered are three coffins: one black, one wooden, and one ornate, positioned horizontally and vertically; the black one is displayed on a stand. In front of the coffins lies a large green funeral wreath with two white birds and a purple ribbon inscribed with the name "Joe." To the right, two silver candelabra with white candles support a blue funeral wreath. Near the candelabra are two gray coffins bearing engraved plates, one with the names BAKER, RAKE, BURLE, BROOKE, GRAVE, and HALL 1911. There is a purple urn on a pedestal against the wall. Suspended from the ceiling, a large colorful stained-glass panel is held in a wooden frame, and a box labeled "COFFIN LINNING" is above. The ceiling features exposed wooden beams and a green hanging lamp. On the back wall, there is a small room or cabinet with various glass bottles and containers, a fan, and shelves holding vases or embalming supplies. The floor is covered in red tiles, while the walls are light gray with horizontal lines resembling wooden paneling. A skylight is situated above, framed by the beams. Various small objects such as brushes, tools, and a picture frame are also scattered around the room, contributing to the overall mortuary setting.
title: Garage of Funeral Parlor, 1917
